newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Sao Paulo state, Brasilia sign major debt deal.
newsitem.headline: Sao Paulo state, Brasilia sign major debt deal.

text.p: Sao Paulo state and the federal government signed an accord to refinance 37 billion reais ($35.8 billion) of state debt and sell 51 percent of state bank Banespa to the federal government, an official said.
Sao Paulo Governor Mario Covas said the price of the 51 percent Banespa stake would be determined within a year by federal and state officials.
The deal, signed by Covas and Finance Ministry officials, still needs approval from federal and state lawmakers.

Most of Sao Paulo's debt, some 20 billion reais is owed to Banespa. The bank, Brazil's largest state development bank, has been under Central Bank management since December 1994 due to financial problems.
Under the agreement, Sao Paulo would pay off 20 percent of its total debt, about 7.5 billion reais ($7.3 billion), with asset sales.
The remaining 80 percent, about 29.5 billion reais ($28.5 billion), would be financed over a 30-year period at an interest rate of six percent plus inflation.

In addition to Sao Paulo's obligations to Banespa, the deal covers the state's debt to state bank Nossa Caixa Nosso Banco and obligations in the form of government securities. The agreement covers all state debt through March 31, 1996, when it totaled 37 billion reais.
Officials say Sao Paulo's debt has grown to about 42 billion reais since then.
The deal allows Sao Paulo to regain control of Banespa within a year if it pays off half of its 20 billion real debt to the bank, Covas said.
Most analysts, however, think the state does not have the money to hold on to the bank.
The terms of the deal are similar to packages reached in September with Minas Gerais and Rio Grande do Sul states, for 8.6 billion reais and 6.0 billion reais, respectively.
